thesis: Desert Bloom sells one machine, the K8, and it sells it through one person's conversation: Kara explains the water, answers questions, then reviews pricing and financing, and the site is organised as that conversation rather than as a shop or a catalogue. After the fixed opening, the home page turns back to the water and follows the order of the call: your water, how it reaches the glass, what filtration plus electrolysis does, what happens after the conversation, who you will speak to, where it is available. Every picture is a doorway, so media is cut as arches and arch seams rather than rectangles, and the only dark moments are a quiet video of water in a glass and a short strip of plain promises. There is no price grid and no calculator because the offer is reviewed in person, and the single money amount appears once, in the closing section.
